biggest_catch: No fixed pay: you set your own rates and keep 80% after Rover's 20% fee, but bookings are not guaranteed — earnings depend entirely on demand, competition, pricing, and reviews in your area.
catches: Rover takes a 20% service fee per booking in the US (sitters keep 80%); fees vary by country.
Sitters set their own rates, so there is no fixed pay: earnings depend on local demand, pricing, reviews, and response speed.
A non-refundable profile review fee may be charged at signup.
You must be 18+, pass identity verification, and abide by local laws; sitters are independent contractors with no guaranteed bookings.
Payment arrives ~2 days after the service completes, not instantly.

steps: Create a Rover account and start a service-provider (sitter/walker) profile.
Complete identity verification, build your profile (experience, photos), take the safety quiz, and request testimonials.
Pass Rover's manual profile review (Rover manually reviews all profiles before listing).
Set your own rates and availability for boarding, house sitting, day care, walks, and drop-ins.
Accept booking requests from pet owners; owners pay via Rover at booking; you are paid ~2 days after the service completes.
timing: Profile approval takes a few days; payment ~2 days after each completed service.
